Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.",
  "Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.",
  "Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.",
  "If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.",
  "Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.",
  "Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.",
  "Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000."
]

You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.",
  "The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.",
  "The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.",
  "Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.",
  "Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.",
  "Indemnification obligations are uncapped.",
  "Gross negligence is uncapped.",
  "Wilful misconduct is uncapped.",
  "Fraud is uncapped.",
  "Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.",
  "Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.",
  "The cap is based on 12 months of fees.",
  "Indemnification obligations are uncapped.",
  "Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.",
  "Gross negligence is uncapped.",
  "Wilful misconduct is uncapped."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"fallback","mappings":[{"element":"The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.","status":"already_met","quote":"COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR."},{"element":"The cap is based on 12 months of fees.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[2]},{"element":"Indemnification obligations are uncapped.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1,3]},{"element":"Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1,3]},{"element":"Gross negligence is uncapped.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1,3]},{"element":"Wilful misconduct is uncapped.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1,3]}]}

Finding rationale:
Section 7(a) caps both parties, so mutuality is satisfied, and 7(b) excludes lost profits and indirect/consequential damages mutually. The clause nonetheless fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the basis is total fees paid for the relevant Services rather than 12 months' fees, so on a short or front-loaded engagement Contractor's exposure can fall below six months' fees; and (ii) there is no usable carve-out — the sole exception points to "PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF", which in this document is the Independent Contractor clause and not an indemnity, so indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap. Our edit re-bases both caps to fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and adds a mutual, expressly uncapped Excluded Claims definition, while preserving the existing Paragraph 9 exception (which benefits us) verbatim. Contractor's cap remains scoped to Services under a Statement of Work while Company's covers the Agreement generally; that asymmetry favours us and is left unchanged. Preferred-only items (USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", data protection/security, fraud and IP carve-outs, and payment obligations outside the cap) are noted but not pressed.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0035: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
p0036: (b) NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

Resolved definitions:
Agreement: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Contractor: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Services: (a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. In all instances of a conflict, between the provisions of this Agreement and the specific provisions set forth in a Statement of Work, the provisions of this Agreement shall control.

Rendered operative language:
(a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF AND EXCLUDED CLAIMS, WHICH ARE UNCAPPED FOR EITHER PARTY, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM.
"EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, AND ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT.
(b) NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] We have re-based each party's cap to fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim (Contractor's cap remains scoped to Services under a Statement of Work) and added mutual Excluded Claims — indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct — outside the cap, keeping the existing Paragraph 9 exception intact. This is our fallback liability position.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."

**Finding submitted: deviation (INSURANCE), fallback target.**

- **What exists:** § 14 (p0048) is a real insurance clause — workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, professional E&O of USD 1,000,000, plus certificates/evidence of insurance and notice of material change on Company's request. The fallback E&O element is already met verbatim, so I did not redraft it.
- **What fails:** No cyber/privacy coverage anywhere in the document, while Contractor obtains Company Confidential Information (p0038) and may access Company computer systems and facilities (§ 1(c)). That is a material fallback failure.
- **Cure:** One `insert_after` adding a single sentence with the fallback USD 2,000,000 cyber and privacy limit — no changes to the untouched coverages, no volunteered preferred-level limits, tails, or at-own-expense language.
- **Noted, not flagged:** absence of a CGL aggregate figure, E&O at USD 1M rather than the preferred USD 2M, and no one-year post-term tail — these are preferred-only shortfalls recorded in the rationale.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.",
  "Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.",
  "Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.",
  "If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.",
  "Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.",
  "Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.",
  "Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"fallback","mappings":[{"element":"Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.","status":"already_met","quote":"professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)"},{"element":"Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
Section 14 contains a usable insurance clause: workers' compensation as required by statute, CGL of USD 1,000,000, professional E&O of USD 1,000,000, and certificates/evidence of insurance on Company's request. It therefore already satisfies the fallback E&O element (USD 1,000,000) and several preferred elements. However, it contains no cyber/privacy coverage at all, and Contractor obtains Company Confidential Information ("all documents, software, reports, data, records, forms ... obtained by Contractor from Company") and may access Company computer systems and facilities under §1(c). The clause accordingly fails the fallback on the cyber element (USD 2,000,000), so we propose the single shortest addition at the fallback level. Shortfalls against the preferred position only (no CGL aggregate figure, E&O at USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000, no post-term tail) are noted but not redlined.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0048: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

Category: transition

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

**Finding: missing (TRANSITION) — redline proposed and submitted.**

- **Investigation:** Read §6 (Termination), §4 (Ownership/materials), §1, §5 and §7 (including the stray §6(c) at p0044 and the confidentiality clause at p0038–p0040). Keyword search returned no hits for data return/export/deletion/transition; the document has no defined "Customer Data".
- **Gap:** The only wind-down obligations are payment of accrued fees and assignment of Works in progress. There is no transition assistance, no data return/export, and no deletion obligation — failing both preferred and fallback.
- **Cure:** One insert as new §6(d) carrying exactly the six preferred elements: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return of Company Data (defined inline to reach all data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for us) in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion **after** that return. No survival tails, procedures, or other non-element boilerplate added; existing paragraphs untouched.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Document: 1. PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-4f03f256","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.","rationale":"Section 7 is captioned \"INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR\" but contains no indemnity language at all: 7(a)-(c) are only liability caps, a damages exclusion and a fee waiver, and a full-document search for \"indemn\" returns nothing except that heading. The only IP hook is the non-infringement warranty in 5(c), which gives no defence, indemnity or remedies, and 7(a)'s exception points to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), a dangling carve-out. With no Contractor IP indemnity this sits in walk-away territory, so we insert the fallback-level Contractor IP indemnity (usual Company modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace and refund remedies, 3x annual fees super-cap) and conform the 7(a) cap so it does not swallow that super-cap. We did not add a Company-side indemnity, since none exists today and adding one would only weaken us.","proposal":"Insert Contractor IP indemnity with standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap; conform the liability cap exception.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-f13b8afc","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.","rationale":"The ownership bargain sits at or above our fallback and no redline is warranted. Section 4(a) vests all SOW work product (the \"Works\", expressly including data, computer programs and documentation) in Clear Capital, conditioned only on the work having been invoiced and paid — consistent with our position that we own what we pay for — and §6(b)/§7(c) add an express \"hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress\". Section 4(b) leaves RadialSpark with its own pre-existing proprietary tools, methodologies and know-how, which is acceptable, and §4(c) gives us a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use, copy and modify any Contractor's Information embedded in the Works for our business operations, reinforced by §4(d) (we may make changes ourselves or through third parties without further payment). No Clear Capital IP or data is assigned or licensed to RadialSpark: §5(b) carves out \"rights respecting programs, data and materials provided by Company\", and §8 bars Contractor from using or disclosing our Confidential Information (expressly including Company records and data) without our express prior written permission, so there is no standing Vendor data licence to narrow. There is no joint ownership in the document. Short of preferred only in minor respects we note but do not flag: the §4(c) licence is not labelled \"irrevocable\" or \"worldwide\", and there is no standalone sentence declaring that we retain all rights in Clear Capital data.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-cc4b6c63","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1 PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.","rationale":"No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Clear Capital anywhere in the Agreement. The engagement is expressly task-by-task through individually agreed Statements of Work (§ 1(a)), with no requirements commitment, minimum volume, or prohibition on procuring comparable services from third parties; § 3 compensation is purely time-and-materials per SOW and is not tied to exclusive engagement. The only uses of \"exclusive\" are Contractor's ownership of its pre-existing materials (§ 4, p0020), a non-exclusive licence in our favour (p0021), and the entire-agreement clause (p0051) — none of which restrict our sourcing freedom. The sole restrictive covenant is a mutual non-solicitation of employees (p0047), which is not exclusivity. This meets the preferred position; no redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-be47251f","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 6 TERMINATION.","rationale":"The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-damages, minimum-fee or early-termination-fee construct payable by Clear Capital. Termination is available to either party for any or no reason on 15 days' notice (§ 6(a)) and on uncured material breach (§ 6(b)), and the only payment consequence in §§ 6(b) and 7(c) is Contractor's actual fees and expenses \"incurred or earned … through the effective date of such termination\" — compensation for work actually performed, not a liquidated amount. Compensation (§ 3) is time-and-materials with no late-payment penalty, non-refundable minimum, or termination charge; the non-solicitation clause (§ 13) carries no placement or buy-out fee; and § 7 caps liability by reference to fees paid rather than stipulating damages. This meets the preferred position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties, so no redline is proposed. Noted only for completeness: § 5's anti-bribery clause and the liability caps operate in our favour or neutrally and are not liquidated-damages exposure.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-6d55ddef","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.","rationale":"The only licence grant is Section 4(c). It is helpfully perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable, and is not revocable at Contractor's discretion, so this is not walk-away territory. However, \"Company\" is defined as Clear Capital alone (preamble) with no affiliate coverage or notice path, and Section 10 bars either party from assigning or transferring the Agreement without consent, with no successor carve-out, so the licence fails both fallback elements (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor). We therefore target the fallback with one short sentence appended to Section 4(c), leaving the grant language and the general assignment clause otherwise untouched. Preferred-level items (express irrevocability, named contractor use) are noted but not pursued given the existing perpetual, sublicensable grant.","proposal":"Add affiliate coverage on written notice and successor transferability to the Section 4(c) licence.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-2fa27ca2","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.","rationale":"The agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity, territory or field-of-use covenant binding Company: § 1 (purpose/scope), § 4 (ownership), § 6 (termination) and § 7 (general terms) impose no limit on the businesses Company may operate or the products it may buy, build or license, and searches for \"compete/competitor\", \"exclusive/exclusivity/restriction\" and \"shall not\" return nothing of that character. The two use-limiting provisions are out of scope for this rule: (i) p0020 (\"Company shall not resell or make use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives under this Agreement\") is licence scope over Contractor's own pre-existing materials and records, not a restriction on Company's own products, brand or business — and p0021 in fact grants Company a perpetual, sublicensable licence over Contractor's Information incorporated into the Works for Company's business operations; and (ii) p0047 is a mutual one-year employee non-solicit, an employment covenant that binds Vendor equally and is not a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on our business. The preferred position (\"Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction\") is therefore satisfied on the document as drafted, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-47014adb","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.","rationale":"Section 10 is the only assignment provision; there is no change-of-control trigger anywhere (Section 6 termination rights are mutual for convenience and breach, not change of control), so no Vendor exit right needs deletion. The clause is mutual and applies a reasonableness standard to consent, but it subjects every assignment, including an assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, to the Contractor's prior consent. That fails the fallback requirement of a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, so we have added that carve-out only, leaving the existing consent and reasonableness mechanics (which already satisfy the remaining fallback elements) untouched.","proposal":"Add mutual successor-assignment carve-out with written notice to the nonassignability clause.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-9d86ac71","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3 CONTRACTOR'S COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The agreement grants RadialSpark no audit, inspection, verification or usage-review right against Clear Capital. Compensation is time-and-materials, verified through Contractor's own invoices and supporting detail (§ 3(b)), and the only access provisions run the other way — Contractor's personnel must comply with Company's security and system-access policies when at a Company facility (§ 1(c)). Searches for audit, inspection, records, verification, compliance monitoring and system access return nothing, and §§ 1, 3 and 4 contain no such right. Because there is no Vendor audit right to constrain, the AUDIT rule's frequency, notice, off-site, auditor-independence, cost-allocation and no-system-access limits are unnecessary; the absence of any audit right is more protective than either the preferred or fallback position. We therefore do not propose inserting audit machinery against ourselves.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-b3f0a2a3","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.","rationale":"Governing law is Arizona, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the clause fails both the preferred and fallback positions. In addition, Section 19 subjects all Disputes to mandatory binding arbitration under the U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules rather than to a court forum, and there is no venue or jurisdiction provision anywhere in the Agreement. We have therefore moved the governing law to New York and converted the arbitration mechanic into exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, and conformed the Section 19 heading so no arbitration mechanic is left dangling.","proposal":"Move governing law to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive New York County court jurisdiction","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-25a09cbd","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3 CONTRACTOR'S COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The compensation provisions (§ 3) set rates and invoicing solely by Statement of Work, and searches across the full agreement (including §§ 1, 3-7) return no most-favoured-nation, best-price, price-matching, benchmarking or \"no less favourable terms\" mechanic of any kind. Company therefore has no obligation to extend Contractor terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers, which satisfies the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation). Contractor's unilateral right to change rates on 30 days' notice in § 3(b) is a pricing-flexibility point, not an MFN obligation, and is outside this rule. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-e0cf90fe","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3 CONTRACTOR'S COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, volume or take-or-pay commitment on Clear Capital, and there are no shortfall or usage-cap mechanics anywhere (searches for \"minimum\", commitment, volume, shortfall and take-or-pay return nothing). Services are engaged \"on a task by task basis\" under Statements of Work (§ 1(a)) and compensation is strictly time-and-materials as set out in each SOW plus actual expenses (§ 3(a)), so we pay only for services we order and consume. On termination, Contractor is paid only \"all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned\" through the effective date (§ 6(b)), confirming no residual committed spend. This meets the preferred position; no redline required. Note only that rate changes on 30 days' notice (§ 3(b)) are a pricing point handled under a separate rule, not a volume commitment.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-32d65825","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.","rationale":"Section 13 is the only solicitation restriction in the document and it binds Clear Capital as well as RadialSpark. It already satisfies two fallback elements (it is mutual and limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services) and it is a solicitation-only restraint, not a no-hire. It fails the fallback on two material terms: the period runs for the whole term plus one year after termination rather than twelve (12) months from the end of the person's involvement (potentially far longer than 12 months for personnel involved early), and there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches — the \"express written consent\" softener is not equivalent. We therefore re-anchor the duration to twelve (12) months after involvement ends and add the two carve-outs, leaving the rest of the clause verbatim.","proposal":"Limit the mutual non-solicit to twelve (12) months after the person's involvement ends and add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-renewal-2b8687fd","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1 PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.","rationale":"There is no auto-renewal anywhere in the Agreement. Section 2 (p0011) creates an evergreen term running until terminated under Section 6, and Section 6(a) (p0032) lets either party — including us — terminate for any or no reason on 15 days' notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding, i.e. well inside the preferred 30-day opt-out. New work only arises by mutually executed Statements of Work (p0004: \"Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties\"), so continued engagement effectively requires mutual written agreement rather than an automatic renewal. Because renewal is not automatic, the conditional automatic-renewal elements (12-month renewal term, 60-day Vendor reminder) and the renewal price-uplift cap are not engaged, and there is no non-renewal notice window to shorten. Noted but not flagged here: Section 3(b) (p0014) gives Contractor a unilateral right to change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap; that is a mid-term pricing mechanic rather than a renewal uplift and belongs to the pricing rule, not RENEWAL. No redline proposed under this rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-e5ba94f3","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 6 TERMINATION.","rationale":"The Agreement runs indefinitely until terminated under Paragraph 6 (p0011), and the only convenience right in Section 6(a) is available solely \"At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding.\" We therefore have no right to exit an active engagement without cause, and no prepaid-fee refund mechanic; the remainder of Section 6 is cause-based only and Section 3 contains no early-termination fee. This fails both the preferred and the fallback Customer-side elements, so we add a Company-only convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Contractor's side already conforms: its convenience right cannot be exercised while a Statement of Work is outstanding, so it cannot walk away from committed work (we note that the 15-day notice in the no-SOW shell period is shorter than our preferred 90 days, which we flag but do not redline).","proposal":"Add a Company-only convenience termination right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-8198282b","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 6 TERMINATION.","rationale":"Section 6 and the stray Section 6(c) at p0044 address only final payment and assignment of Works in progress; nothing in Sections 1, 4, 5, 6 or 7 (including the confidentiality clause at p0038-p0040) requires Contractor to provide transition assistance, to return or export our data, or to delete it after return.
